components: Genuinely open 30-EC third-year minor/profiling space: the OER permits an approved general or movement-science minor; no particular optional sport or clinical minor is assumed.

Required 24 EC research project. Research is conducted in teams of at least two, with individual reports and a joint presentation and defence. Entry requires all first-year courses, Statistics, and the specified measurement-course practical and written-exam results.

audience.programmeDescription: Students investigate human movement in sport, health and rehabilitation through anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, neuroscience, psychology, measurement and data analysis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination combines functional anatomy and physiology with the neural control of perception and action, quantitative measurement and health research. VU adds gait and force analysis, exercise testing, motor learning, biomechanics and sport performance.

curriculum.limitation: The 180-EC programme contains 120 EC of required first- and second-year courses, a further 6-EC anatomy course, 30 EC of open choice and a 24-EC research project. No particular optional sport, health or clinical minor is assumed. The research project requires all first-year courses, a passed Statistics course, the passed practical assessment in Measuring Physical Quantities and at least 4.0 on its written examination. Research is conducted in teams of at least two, with an individual report and a joint presentation and defence; the individual report has a second assessor. The proposal must be approved before measurements begin. Required practicals and assignments apply to the relevant courses. The Dutch diagnostic test and any required remediation add no separate credits. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC, with the specified minimum examination results in Biomechanics and Mathematics, subject to exceptions. Open choice is subject to level, approval and overlap rules; free electives require at least 12 EC at level 300, while an individually composed minor must be coherent and contain no more than one introductory course.

componentNotes.y3-03: 24 EC of supervised research conducted in teams of at least two, with individual reports and a joint presentation and defence; specified entry requirements apply.

core: Functional anatomy, exercise physiology and movement-related health
Neural control, perception and development of action
Measurement, mathematics, computing and statistics for movement research
Clinical movement difficulty, rehabilitation and research interpretation
adjacent: Sport psychology, emotion, motivation and movement-related mental health
Athletic training load and performance physiology
questions: How can anatomy, neural control and measurement explain altered movement?
How do psychological health and behaviour shape movement and recovery?
How do athletes adapt to training load and avoid overtraining?
